description: Conformance manifest for the W2-F internal service-delegation example fixtures (ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION — v0.1.0, not stable v1/GA). 'kind' drives the expected validation outcome: positive = MUST validate; negative-schema = MUST fail JSON Schema validation; negative-semantic = MUST validate structurally but MUST be rejected by a relying-party trust invariant a schema alone cannot enforce (a fixed test clock NOW=1900000000 makes the time/replay/mismatch checks deterministic). Schema paths are relative to contracts/json-schema/; fixture paths are relative to contracts/examples/svc/. Validated by tools/contract-validation/validate-svc.mjs.

examples.invariant: SI-3 REPLAY KEY REQUIRED: claims.jti is required (RFC 7519 §4.1.7); a token with no unique id has no anti-replay key and is rejected.
SI-4 SENDER-CONSTRAINED: claims.cnf is required (RFC 8705 §3.1); a non-certificate-bound (bearer) token is rejected — it could be replayed without the bound key.
SI-4 SENDER-CONSTRAINED: cnf['x5t#S256'] must be a 43-char base64url SHA-256 thumbprint; a malformed thumbprint is rejected — the mTLS binding cannot be evaluated against garbage.
SI-1 ASYMMETRIC-ONLY: header.alg must be in the jwtAlg enum (asymmetric only); a shared-secret HS256 token is rejected (RFC 8725 §3.1/§3.2).
SI-1 ASYMMETRIC-ONLY: header.alg 'none' is not in the jwtAlg enum; an unsecured token is structurally impossible (RFC 8725 §3.2; RFC 9068 §4).
SI-7 NO STATIC BEARER: additionalProperties=false rejects an inline 'authorization' static bearer; authority is the short-lived certificate-bound token, never a long-lived shared secret.

SI-8 NO FORWARDED USER TOKEN: additionalProperties=false rejects an 'on_behalf_of_user_token' field; delegation is expressed by the act/actor claims (RFC 8693), never by smuggling an end-user token through the seam.

SR-1 TIME WINDOW: claims.exp (1899990000) is before the test clock NOW (1900000000). The relying party MUST reject an expired token even though the signature verifies. Structurally valid — epoch values are well-formed.
SR-1 TIME WINDOW: claims.nbf (1900010000) is after NOW; the token is not-yet-valid and MUST be rejected (RFC 7519 §4.1.5).

SR-2 SHORT TTL: exp - iat = 3700s exceeds the 120s hard ceiling (svc-trust-metadata.max_token_ttl_seconds const 120). The relying party MUST reject an over-long-lived token even if it is currently within its window.

SR-3 AUDIENCE: token.aud ('svc:cyber-ai-inference') != relying_party.audience ('svc:soc-notifier'). A token presented to any audience other than its own MUST be rejected (confused-deputy defense; RFC 9700 §2.3).
SR-4 CROSS-TENANT: body tenant_id ('tenant-globex') != token cybrik.tenant_id ('tenant-acme'). Authoritative tenant derives from the token; the advisory body never elevates. MUST be rejected.
SR-5 ORG SCOPE: body org_scope ('org:globex/soc/tier1') != token cybrik.org_scope ('org:acme/soc/tier2'). The advisory org hint MUST match the token; it carries no authority on its own.

SR-6 OPERATION BINDING: body operation.name ('ai.summarization.create') != token cybrik.operation.name ('ai.inference.create'). A body requesting an operation the token did not authorize is a confused-deputy attempt and MUST be rejected.

SR-7 MARKING NON-ESCALATION: body data_marking (restricted/TLP:RED) is above token cybrik.marking (confidential/TLP:AMBER) on the classification/TLP lattice. The relying party MUST reject a request above the token's authorized marking ceiling.

SR-8 REPLAY: the presented token reuses jti 'jti-soc-9f8e7d6c5b4a3210' already seen on the positive request. A second presentation of the same jti MUST be rejected by the relying party's replay cache (schema cannot track cross-request state).
